key_concepts: Constellations are groups of stars that form distinct patterns
Some constellations are visible only in summer or winter
Polaris is visible in the night sky throughout the year
Polaris is also known as the North Star
Polaris is part of the constellation Ursa Minor
The Big Dipper and Little Dipper are asterisms, not constellations
Cassiopeia forms a letter W and represents a queen
Orion is a prominent constellation named after a hunter
Ursa Major resembles a big bear and is one of the largest constellations
Draco means the dragon and is one of the largest constellations
Navigators use Polaris as a guide for determining directions
